subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: When you wave a sparkler quickly in the dark, you briefly see a continuous trail of light rather than separate points — because the visual impression persists for a fraction of a second after the stimulus is gone. This very brief, high-capacity initial memory store is called:
explanation: Sensory memory holds an almost exact copy of sensory input for a very brief moment before it decays or is passed to short-term memory — the first of the three memory stages.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch10 — Three-Stage Memory Model (Complete)
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: According to the classic Atkinson-Shiffrin multi-store model of memory, information flows through which sequence of stores?

options.option_text: Sensory memory → Short-term memory → Long-term memory
Long-term memory → Short-term memory → Sensory memory
Short-term memory → Sensory memory → Long-term memory
There is only one single memory store with no distinct stages

explanation: Information first enters sensory memory, then with attention passes to short-term/working memory, and finally with rehearsal to long-term memory.
